messages:
Alice: Heads-up — AMS edge IP fabric had a BGP flap at ~09:12 UTC. We saw about 18-22% of GPU nodes in the AMS slice go into Unreachable and tail latency spiked for a few routes. infra-bot posted alerts and some traffic shifted automatically to LAX and AMS-fallback pools.
Dana: Oncall here, ack. I kicked off the manual weighted-shift to LAX to even things out, monitoring now. No user-facing errors reported yet, mostly higher token latencies on longer sequences.
infra-bot: [alert] BGP_SESSION_DOWN: ams-rr-2 -> route-reflector (09:12:07 UTC)
Ben: I validated node health and kube events — lots of `NetworkUnreachable` on the node NICs and some kube-proxy flaps. `kubectl get nodes` showed NotReady for ~9 nodes in ams-gpu-slice-2.
Carlos: Looking at the fabric: new route-reflector config pushed 09:05 UTC from netops; there are withdrawn prefixes and a high churn in RIB. I can see the same ASN pulling routes every 30s. Likely config bug causing withdraw/announce loops.
Alice: OK — immediate: (1) keep traffic shifted off affected AMS slice until netops stabilizes, (2) ensure autoscaler in that slice is paused to avoid thrash, (3) add a short-term sticky to avoid bouncing sessions. Dana can you make the sticky change?
Dana: Done — added hold for 90s and paused autoscaler for ams-gpu-slice-2.
Frank: For the future playbook: we should add a step to pre-warm reserve capacity in at least one other region before applying RR changes during business hours. Also we need an automated detect->dry-run shift so we can validate route health before moving live traffic.
Emma: Can we get a quick delta on cost impact for the shift? We moved ~30% of steady traffic from AMS to LAX for ~2h. Need that for postmortem.
Ben: Rough calc: 30% shift * 2h * avg token/min costs = estimating ~ $4.2k of incremental network egress/GPU cost. I'll refine numbers with billing.
Carlos: Netops will roll back the RR config now. They want us to confirm zero prefixes withdrawn for 5m before we re-allow traffic back. Suggestion: add route_health_check probe and tie it to the routing policy.
Alice: Agreed. Action items for runbook update (quick list we can use in post-incident):
- Add pre-change checklist for netops pushes that impact AMs fabric (include route-health-check and a canary RR node).
- Add a traffic-shift dry-run command in the playbook: `redwood shift --dry-run --from=ams --to=lax --pct=10 --verify=route_health` and a 5m watch.
- Document cost guardrails and automated notify to finance when shift >20% for >1h.
- Define autoscaler pause behavior during region-level network instability (default pause 5m).
- Add a scheduled weekly 'failover dry-run' to exercise weighted routing and observe tail latencies.
Carlos: I'll PR the route-health-check probe into infra-monitoring and add it to the routing policy.
Frank: Also recommend an improvement: when BGP flaps are detected, don't immediately shift 100% traffic — prefer a staged ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% with health gates. Adds a small delay but prevents overload in target regions.
Dana: Note: during this incident we had a confusion about ownership for `hold-sticky` vs `autoscaler pause`. We should put clear owners per step in the playbook (SRE vs Infra vs NetOps).
Alice: Good call. Assign owners in playbook: NetOps = route changes, SRE = traffic shift + autoscaler/roll logic, Infra = probes/monitoring.
Emma: Recording requirements: need a single-line summary for customers and a more detailed timeline for eng. I'll assemble a 1-paragraph external summary once we have the action items confirmed.
Ben: I'll attach kube and node logs to the postmortem doc and include the billing numbers.
Carlos: NetOps rollback successful at 09:39 UTC, RR churn subsided. Still watching RIB for 5m as requested.
infra-bot: [info] ROUTE_STABLE: ams-rr-2 (09:44:21 UTC)
Dana: Re-enabled autoscaler for ams-gpu-slice-2 and started slow traffic ramp-back following Frank's staged ramp proposal. Observed no new errors.
Alice: Closing loop: let's make these concrete post-incident action items and update the failover playbook. I'll open the incident doc and tag owners: Ben (logs + billing), Carlos (route probe + PR), Frank (runbook ramp + automation), Dana (oncall notes + playbook steps), Emma (external comms).
Frank: I'll prototype the `redwood shift --dry-run` helper this week and put a short RFC on the runbook repo.
Emma: Thanks — please ping me when PRs are up so I can include links in the external note.
Alice: Thanks everyone — good catch and smooth coordinated response. We'll use this to tighten the failover procedures.
